messages:
laura: FYI found a customer report: resumed streaming plus a prefetch sidecar produced two confirmed token charges for the same prefix. repro attached.
aj: ugh. paste logs? want to see if the router and prefetch each wrote a provisional then both confirmed.
laura: logs:
```
2026-03-21T15:42:10.123Z [router] lvl=info route=resume session=xyz prefix=64 event=provisional_charge id=tx-R1
2026-03-21T15:42:10.128Z [sidecar-prefetch] lvl=info session=xyz prefix=64 event=provisional_charge id=tx-P1
2026-03-21T15:42:10.129Z [ledger] lvl=info session=xyz id=tx-R1 event=confirm tokens=64
2026-03-21T15:42:10.130Z [ledger] lvl=info session=xyz id=tx-P1 event=confirm tokens=64
```
laura: both provisional ids end up confirmed; ledger sums them.
chip: that matches a race where prefetch doesn't check router-claimed flag. two distinct provisional ids => double confirm.
maria: can you query events to show ordering with trace ids?
```
SELECT event_ts, source, event, tx_id
FROM token_events
WHERE session='xyz'
ORDER BY event_ts;
```
vik: console trace shows router.trace_id=tr-R and sidecar.trace_id=tr-P. they are different but share session. ops-bot: billing alert created: billing-discrepancy session=xyz delta=+64 tokens.
aj: root causes to consider:
- prefetch should be idempotent w.r.t. prefix charge if router already reserved tokens
- ledger should dedupe confirms when provisional ranges overlap for same session
- console should surface provisional vs confirmed per session so ops can spot duplicates quickly
chip: ledger dedupe is tricky because provisional ids are unique and may legitimately confirm twice for different prefixes. dedupe rule would need to consider session + prefix range overlap + time window.
maria: UX: add a per-request timeline view in the console that lists provisional events, which worker created them, and confirm events. right now we only show aggregated counts which hides the duplication.
laura: quick mitigation: make prefetch write provisional with a special low-priority tag; confirmation requires a router-grant handshake unless the provisional is older than N ms.
aj: alternative short term: sidecar checks an in-memory session marker (cheap) before issuing provisional. if marker exists skip charge. but multi-zone races mean eventual window where both see no marker.
chip: long-term: assign canonical authorizer for prefix claims — router wins by default. sidecars must attempt a fast RPC to router to get claim token; if RPC times out treat as no-claim and skip provisional (we accept some lost prefetch counting).
vik: we'll need a canary plan so this mitigation doesn't undercount real usage. Ops: surface a temporary "prefetch-skip" metric to check dropped prefetch confirms.
maria: I'll draft a console patch to show provisional ids under the session trace and diff against confirmed. also add a flag in the billing UI to filter by provisional/confirmed.
laura: I'll open RFC: include reproducer, gap analysis, mitigation PR for sidecar guard, and ledger dedupe design notes. aiming to ship a canary next week.
aj: for SLO/alerts: create a short-lived alert when confirmed_tokens - max(provisional_by_canonical) > threshold in last 5m. billing-bot: created alert rule: diff_token_spike(session).
chip: cc @infra: if we introduce short RPC from sidecars to router for claim we need to ensure it doesn't add tail latency to resume path. sidecar should do non-blocking best-effort.
laura: thanks all. pairing welcome on the repro. will paste the reproduce script in the RFC. :thumbsup:
